    def __init__(
    self,
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    max_iter: int = 100,
    tol: float = 1e-5,
    alpha: float = 1e-6,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias, name, trainable)
    if alpha < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"alpha must be non-negative, got {alpha}.")
    if tol <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"tol must be positive, got {tol}.")
    if max_iter < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"max_iter must be a positive integer, got {max_iter}.")
    self.max_iter = max_iter
    self.tol = tol
    self.alpha = alpha
    self.use_float64 = use_float64
    self.gram_dtype = gram_dtype

    def solve(
    self,
    states: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
    """Solve ridge regression via Conjugate Gradient on flattened inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        Flattened state matrix of shape `(N, in_features)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Flattened target matrix of shape `(N, out_features)`.

    Returns
    -------
    coefs : torch.Tensor
        Coefficient matrix of shape `(in_features, out_features)`.
    intercept : torch.Tensor or None
        Intercept vector of shape `(out_features,)`, or `None` when
        the layer was built with `bias=False` (the ridge problem is
        then solved without centering, i.e. with no intercept).
    """
    return self._solve_ridge_cg(states, targets, self.alpha)

    RidgeReadoutLayer ¶

    RidgeReadoutLayer(
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    alpha: float = 1e-06,
    solver: str = "cholesky",
    state_noise: float = 0.0,
    noise_draws: int | None = None,
    noise_seed: int | None = None,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: dtype | None = None,
)

    Bases: ReadoutLayer

    Readout layer with a direct ridge-regression solver.

    For the readout widths typical of reservoir computing (in_features = 100–2000) the (F, F) Gram matrix factorises exactly and almost instantly. A direct Cholesky solve is both faster and exact (up to floating point), whereas CGReadoutLayer only approximates the solution and can under-converge on the ill-conditioned concatenated-input readouts produced by ott_esn / power_augmented.

    The solver minimises the same ridge objective as CGReadoutLayer,

    \[ \lVert X W - Y \rVert_2^2 + \alpha \lVert W \rVert_2^2 , \]

    by forming the regularised normal equations (XᵀX + αI) W = Xᵀy and solving them with one of:

    • solver='cholesky' (default) — torch.linalg.cholesky followed by torch.linalg.cholesky_solve. Exploits the symmetric positive definiteness of XᵀX + αI in exact arithmetic for alpha > 0. Finite-precision Gram formation can still lose positive definiteness.
    • solver='solve' — torch.linalg.solve (LU). It does not require positive definiteness, so it supports alpha == 0 on a full-rank Gram.
    Solver-selection guide
    • Default to RidgeReadoutLayer(solver='cholesky') for any well-conditioned readout with alpha > 0 when an explicit normal-equations solve is desired. Runtime and accuracy depend on the workload, precision and hardware. AutoReadoutLayer checks numerical safety and can use the original design matrix instead.
    • Use solver='solve' when you need alpha == 0 (pure least squares) and the Gram is full rank but you don't want the SVD machinery.
    • If the Gram is rank deficient (high-degree NG-RC feature maps, more features than samples), a Cholesky/LU solve will fail or be unstable — reach for SVDReadoutLayer (filter factors) or PinvReadoutLayer (lstsq / pinv) instead.
    Noise-injection / LMNT regularization

    Pass state_noise > 0 to apply state-noise regularization, a standard, tunable tool for closed-loop (autonomous-rollout) robustness rather than only weight magnitude. Fitting on state-noise-perturbed reservoir states mimics the feedback error the model sees when it free-runs on its own output — the injected noise trades a little one-step accuracy for closed-loop stability (Jaeger's state-noise idea; Wikner et al. 2024, Stabilizing machine learning prediction of dynamics, Chaos 34, 043105). It is not a free or automatic forecast-quality win: whether the trade nets out positive is problem- and \(\sigma\)-dependent — it can help or hurt, and \(\sigma\) must be tuned per problem. The shipped default is 0.0 (off); opt in and tune.

    The robust guarantee is the mechanism, not a VPT number: by default (noise_draws=None) the closed-form LMNT (Linearized Multi-Noise Training) path computes the exact analytic expectation of the noise-perturbed Gram — a single scalar on the diagonal (\(N\sigma^2\) raw, \((N-1)\sigma^2\) centered). One solve of the expected normal equations is the infinite-draw limit of the explicit-noise path. This is not the expectation of separately fitted coefficients or chaotic forecasts. Set noise_draws=M to average the normal equations of M explicit Gaussian-perturbed copies before solving once (seeded by noise_seed). This Monte-Carlo path converges to the analytic path as M grows. state_noise is independent of alpha: they add on the diagonal (\(\alpha + N\sigma^2\)) but noise training targets rollout robustness while alpha targets weight norm.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    in_features

    Size of input features (reservoir state dimension).

    TYPE: int

    out_features

    Size of output features (prediction dimension).

    TYPE: int

    bias

    Whether to include a bias term. When True the data is centered and an unpenalised intercept is recovered; when False the raw normal equations are solved with no intercept.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    name

    Name for this readout layer. Used for identification in multi-readout architectures and as the key into targets by ESNTrainer.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

    trainable

    If True, weights are trainable via backpropagation.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    alpha

    L2 regularization strength. Must be non-negative. alpha == 0 is only safe with solver='solve' on a full-rank Gram.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    solver

    Direct solver to use for the normal equations.

    TYPE: (cholesky, solve) DEFAULT: 'cholesky'

    state_noise

    Standard deviation \(\sigma\) of the Gaussian state noise the readout is regularised against for closed-loop stability (see the class docstring). 0.0 (default) disables it — the fit is then byte-identical to a plain ridge solve. Must be non-negative.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.0

    noise_draws

    When state_noise > 0: None (default) uses the closed-form LMNT term (one solve, exact expectation); an integer M >= 1 instead averages M noisy-state normal equations, then solves once (Monte-Carlo). Ignored when state_noise == 0.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: None

    noise_seed

    Seed for the explicit-noise (noise_draws) Gaussian draws, for reproducibility. None uses the process-global RNG. Ignored for the closed-form LMNT path (which is deterministic).

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: None

    use_float64

    If True the small (F, F) factorisation runs in float64 and the result is cast back to the parameter dtype.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    gram_dtype

    Dtype for forming the Gram matrix and right-hand side (the heavy (N, F) matmuls). Default None uses the solve dtype (float64 with use_float64=True) on every device. An explicit gram_dtype=torch.float32 can speed up well-conditioned fits on CUDA, at the cost of precision when forming the normal equations.

    TYPE: dtype DEFAULT: None

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION
    weight

    Weight matrix of shape (out_features, in_features).

    TYPE: Parameter

    bias

    Bias vector of shape (out_features,), or None if bias=False.

    TYPE: Parameter or None

    alpha

    L2 regularization strength.

    TYPE: float

    solver

    The selected direct solver.

    TYPE: str

    state_noise

    Standard deviation of the closed-loop state-noise regulariser.

    TYPE: float

    Examples:

    >>> readout = RidgeReadoutLayer(in_features=200, out_features=3, alpha=1e-6)
>>> states = torch.randn(8, 50, 200)  # (batch, time, features)
>>> targets = torch.randn(8, 50, 3)
>>> readout.fit(states, targets)
>>> output = readout(states)
>>> output.shape
torch.Size([8, 50, 3])

    Closed-form LMNT noise regularisation for closed-loop robustness (the state_noise value below is illustrative — tune it per problem, and expect it to help or hurt depending on the system and \(\sigma\)):

    >>> readout = RidgeReadoutLayer(200, 3, alpha=1e-8, state_noise=1e-3)
    See Also

    CGReadoutLayer : Iterative Conjugate Gradient ridge readout. SVDReadoutLayer : SVD filter-factor readout for rank-deficient Gram. PinvReadoutLayer : lstsq / pseudo-inverse readout. resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer that uses this for fitting.

    def __init__(
    self,
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    alpha: float = 1e-6,
    solver: str = "cholesky",
    state_noise: float = 0.0,
    noise_draws: int | None = None,
    noise_seed: int | None = None,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias, name, trainable)
    if alpha < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"alpha must be non-negative, got {alpha}.")
    if solver not in self._VALID_SOLVERS:
        raise ValueError(f"solver must be one of {self._VALID_SOLVERS}, got {solver!r}.")
    if state_noise < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"state_noise must be non-negative, got {state_noise}.")
    if noise_draws is not None and noise_draws < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"noise_draws must be >= 1 when given, got {noise_draws}.")
    self.alpha = alpha
    self.solver = solver
    self.state_noise = state_noise
    self.noise_draws = noise_draws
    self.noise_seed = noise_seed
    self.use_float64 = use_float64
    self.gram_dtype = gram_dtype

    def solve(
    self,
    states: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
    """Solve ridge regression directly on flattened inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        Flattened state matrix of shape `(N, in_features)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Flattened target matrix of shape `(N, out_features)`.

    Returns
    -------
    coefs : torch.Tensor
        Coefficient matrix of shape `(in_features, out_features)`.
    intercept : torch.Tensor or None
        Intercept vector of shape `(out_features,)`, or `None` when the
        layer was built with `bias=False`.
    """
    if self.state_noise > 0 and self.noise_draws is not None:
        # Explicit Monte-Carlo noise training: average M noisy normal equations.
        generator: torch.Generator | None = None
        if self.noise_seed is not None:
            generator = torch.Generator(device=states.device)
            generator.manual_seed(int(self.noise_seed))
        problem = build_noisy_ridge_problem(
            states,
            targets,
            fit_intercept=self.bias is not None,
            use_float64=self.use_float64,
            gram_dtype=self.gram_dtype,
            state_noise=self.state_noise,
            n_draws=self.noise_draws,
            generator=generator,
        )
    else:
        problem = build_ridge_problem(
            states,
            targets,
            fit_intercept=self.bias is not None,
            use_float64=self.use_float64,
            gram_dtype=self.gram_dtype,
        )
        # Closed-form LMNT: fold the analytic noise-covariance term into the
        # Gram diagonal (no-op when state_noise == 0, keeping the fit exact).
        apply_lmnt_regularizer(problem, self.state_noise)

    layer_name = (
        f"{type(self).__name__}('{self._name}')"
        if self._name is not None
        else type(self).__name__
    )

    if self.solver == "cholesky":
        coefs = solve_ridge(
            problem.gram,
            problem.rhs,
            self.alpha,
            layer_name=layer_name,
            gram_dtype=problem.X.dtype,
        )
    else:  # "solve" — general LU. Does not need positive-definiteness, so
        # it tolerates alpha == 0 on a full-rank Gram; it still benefits
        # from the shared post-solve accuracy residual guard.
        eye = torch.eye(
            problem.n_features,
            dtype=problem.solve_dtype,
            device=problem.gram.device,
        )
        coefs = torch.linalg.solve(problem.gram + self.alpha * eye, problem.rhs)
        _warn_on_precision_loss(
            gram=problem.gram,
            coefs=coefs,
            rhs=problem.rhs,
            alpha_eff=self.alpha,
            cond_estimate=None,
            gram_dtype=problem.X.dtype,
            layer_name=layer_name,
        )

    return finalize_fit(problem, coefs)

    CholeskyReadoutLayer(
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    alpha: float = 1e-06,
    state_noise: float = 0.0,
    noise_draws: int | None = None,
    noise_seed: int | None = None,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: dtype | None = None,
)

    Bases: ReadoutLayer

    Readout layer that solves ridge regression via a Cholesky factorisation.

    The regularised normal equations (XᵀX + αI) W = Xᵀy are formed (with analytic centering when a bias is fitted) and solved with torch.linalg.cholesky followed by torch.cholesky_solve. The (F, F) system is symmetric positive definite for alpha > 0, so the Cholesky factorisation is the fastest, most numerically stable exact solve for the readout widths typical of reservoir computing (in_features = 100–2000).

    Unlike CGReadoutLayer, which only approximates the solution iteratively, this layer returns the exact ridge solution (up to floating point) in a single shot. It is the single-batch counterpart of the streaming IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer: both ultimately Cholesky-solve the same regularised Gram system, so a full-batch CholeskyReadoutLayer fit and an accumulated IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer fit over the same data agree to within floating-point tolerance.

    The solver minimises the same ridge objective as CGReadoutLayer,

    \[ \lVert X W - Y \rVert_2^2 + \alpha \lVert W \rVert_2^2 . \]
    Noise-injection / LMNT regularization

    Pass state_noise > 0 to apply state-noise regularization — a standard, tunable tool for closed-loop (autonomous-rollout) robustness — by training on state-noise-perturbed reservoir states (Jaeger's state noise; Wikner et al. 2024, Chaos 34, 043105). It trades a little one-step accuracy for closed-loop stability; it is not an automatic forecast-quality win (whether it helps or hurts is problem- and \(\sigma\)-dependent, so \(\sigma\) must be tuned per problem — the default is off). The robust guarantee is the mechanism: the default noise_draws=None uses the closed-form LMNT term — the exact analytic expectation of the noisy Gram. Solving these expected normal equations is the infinite-copy limit of explicit-noise training; it does not average separately fitted coefficients. Set noise_draws=M (seeded by noise_seed) to average the normal equations of M noisy copies, then solve once. See RidgeReadoutLayer for the full discussion. 0.0 (default) is byte-identical to a plain fit.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    in_features

    Size of input features (reservoir state dimension).

    TYPE: int

    out_features

    Size of output features (prediction dimension).

    TYPE: int

    bias

    Whether to include a bias term. When True the data is centered and an unpenalised intercept is recovered; when False the raw normal equations are solved with no intercept.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    name

    Name for this readout layer. Used for identification in multi-readout architectures and as the key into targets by ESNTrainer.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

    trainable

    If True, weights are trainable via backpropagation.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    alpha

    L2 regularization strength. Must be non-negative. alpha > 0 guarantees the Gram is positive definite; with alpha == 0 the factorisation succeeds only on a full-rank Gram (reach for SVDReadoutLayer if the Gram may be rank deficient).

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    state_noise

    Standard deviation \(\sigma\) of the closed-loop state-noise regulariser (see the class docstring). 0.0 (default) is byte-identical to a plain fit. Must be non-negative. Adds alpha > 0 positive definiteness insurance too — the LMNT term is a positive diagonal add.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.0

    noise_draws

    None (default) uses the closed-form LMNT term; an integer M >= 1 averages M noisy-state normal equations before one solve. Ignored when state_noise == 0.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: None

    noise_seed

    Seed for the explicit-noise (noise_draws) draws. Ignored for the deterministic LMNT path.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: None

    use_float64

    If True the small (F, F) factorisation runs in float64 and the result is cast back to the parameter dtype.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    gram_dtype

    Dtype for forming the Gram matrix and right-hand side (the heavy (N, F) matmuls). Default None uses the solve dtype (float64 with use_float64=True) on every device. An explicit gram_dtype=torch.float32 can speed up well-conditioned fits on CUDA, at the cost of precision when forming the normal equations.

    TYPE: dtype DEFAULT: None

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION
    weight

    Weight matrix of shape (out_features, in_features).

    TYPE: Parameter

    bias

    Bias vector of shape (out_features,), or None if bias=False.

    TYPE: Parameter or None

    alpha

    L2 regularization strength.

    TYPE: float

    Examples:

    >>> readout = CholeskyReadoutLayer(in_features=200, out_features=3, alpha=1e-6)
>>> states = torch.randn(8, 50, 200)  # (batch, time, features)
>>> targets = torch.randn(8, 50, 3)
>>> readout.fit(states, targets)
>>> output = readout(states)
>>> output.shape
torch.Size([8, 50, 3])

    self,
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,

    super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias, name, trainable)
    if alpha < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"alpha must be non-negative, got {alpha}.")

        raise ValueError(f"state_noise must be non-negative, got {state_noise}.")
    if noise_draws is not None and noise_draws < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"noise_draws must be >= 1 when given, got {noise_draws}.")
    self.alpha = alpha
    self.state_noise = state_noise
    self.noise_draws = noise_draws
    self.noise_seed = noise_seed
    self.use_float64 = use_float64
    self.gram_dtype = gram_dtype

    def solve(
    self,
    states: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
    """Solve ridge regression via a Cholesky factorisation on flattened inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        Flattened state matrix of shape `(N, in_features)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Flattened target matrix of shape `(N, out_features)`.

    Returns
    -------
    coefs : torch.Tensor
        Coefficient matrix of shape `(in_features, out_features)`.
    intercept : torch.Tensor or None
        Intercept vector of shape `(out_features,)`, or `None` when the
        layer was built with `bias=False`.
    """
    if self.state_noise > 0 and self.noise_draws is not None:
        generator: torch.Generator | None = None
        if self.noise_seed is not None:
            generator = torch.Generator(device=states.device)
            generator.manual_seed(int(self.noise_seed))
        problem = build_noisy_ridge_problem(
            states,
            targets,
            fit_intercept=self.bias is not None,
            use_float64=self.use_float64,
            gram_dtype=self.gram_dtype,
            state_noise=self.state_noise,
            n_draws=self.noise_draws,
            generator=generator,
        )
    else:
        problem = build_ridge_problem(
            states,
            targets,
            fit_intercept=self.bias is not None,
            use_float64=self.use_float64,
            gram_dtype=self.gram_dtype,
        )
        apply_lmnt_regularizer(problem, self.state_noise)

    layer_name = (
        f"{type(self).__name__}('{self._name}')"
        if self._name is not None
        else type(self).__name__
    )
    coefs = solve_ridge(
        problem.gram,
        problem.rhs,
        self.alpha,
        layer_name=layer_name,
        gram_dtype=problem.X.dtype,
    )

    return finalize_fit(problem, coefs)

    SVDReadoutLayer ¶

    SVDReadoutLayer(
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    alpha: float = 0.0,
    rcond: float = 1e-15,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: dtype | None = None,
)

    Bases: ReadoutLayer

    Readout layer solved via SVD with Tikhonov filter factors.

    The (optionally centered) design matrix X is decomposed as X = U diag(s) Vᵀ and the ridge solution is reconstructed with filter factors

    \[ W = V \, \operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{s}{s^2 + \alpha}\right) U^\top Y . \]

    For alpha > 0 this is exactly the ridge solution; for alpha == 0 it collapses to the minimum-norm least-squares solution, with singular values at or below an rcond cutoff dropped so a rank-deficient Gram (more features than independent samples, or the near-collinear columns produced by high-degree NG-RC feature maps) is handled gracefully instead of blowing up the way a Cholesky / normal-equations solve would.

    Positive-ridge filter factors are evaluated in scaled form, avoiding overflow from squaring large finite singular values. The requested alpha is preserved; numerical recovery does not add extra regularization.

    Decomposing X directly avoids squaring its condition number by forming XᵀX. This is useful for rank-deficient or ill-conditioned features; attainable accuracy still depends on working precision, data scale and regularization.

    Solver-selection guide
    • Reach for SVDReadoutLayer when the Gram is rank deficient or severely ill-conditioned: alpha == 0 least squares, high-degree NG-RC feature maps, or wide concatenated-input readouts where CG under-converges.
    • Cholesky-based RidgeReadoutLayer can reduce fitting cost when the regularized Gram is well conditioned. Measure accuracy and runtime for the actual matrix shape, dtype and device when choosing a solver.
    • PinvReadoutLayer is the closely-related lstsq / pinv route; SVD here gives explicit control over the Tikhonov filter and rcond.
    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    in_features

    Size of input features (reservoir state dimension).

    TYPE: int

    out_features

    Size of output features (prediction dimension).

    TYPE: int

    bias

    Whether to include a bias term. When True the data is centered and an unpenalised intercept is recovered; when False the raw design matrix is decomposed with no intercept.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    name

    Name for this readout layer. Used for identification in multi-readout architectures and as the key into targets by ESNTrainer.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

    trainable

    If True, weights are trainable via backpropagation.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    alpha

    Tikhonov (L2) regularization strength. Must be finite and non-negative. 0 is fully supported and yields the minimum-norm least-squares solution.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.0

    rcond

    Finite, non-negative relative cutoff for small singular values. Values at or below rcond * s_max are treated as zero (their filter factor is set to zero), which is what makes rank-deficient problems well posed. Only active for alpha == 0; for alpha > 0 the Tikhonov filter already damps small singular values.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-15

    use_float64

    If True the SVD runs in float64 and the result is cast back to the parameter dtype.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    gram_dtype

    Dtype for forming / casting the design matrix. Default None is the solve dtype (float64 with use_float64=True) on every device. No Gram matrix is formed; the decomposition operates directly on the design matrix.

    TYPE: dtype DEFAULT: None

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION
    weight

    Weight matrix of shape (out_features, in_features).

    TYPE: Parameter

    bias

    Bias vector of shape (out_features,), or None if bias=False.

    TYPE: Parameter or None

    alpha

    Tikhonov regularization strength.

    TYPE: float

    rcond

    Relative singular-value cutoff.

    TYPE: float

    Examples:

    >>> readout = SVDReadoutLayer(in_features=200, out_features=3, alpha=0.0)
>>> states = torch.randn(8, 50, 200)  # (batch, time, features)
>>> targets = torch.randn(8, 50, 3)
>>> readout.fit(states, targets)
>>> output = readout(states)
>>> output.shape
torch.Size([8, 50, 3])

    def solve(
    self,
    states: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
    """Solve the readout via SVD filter factors on flattened inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        Flattened state matrix of shape `(N, in_features)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Flattened target matrix of shape `(N, out_features)`.

    Returns
    -------
    coefs : torch.Tensor
        Coefficient matrix of shape `(in_features, out_features)`.
    intercept : torch.Tensor or None
        Intercept vector of shape `(out_features,)`, or `None` when the
        layer was built with `bias=False`.
    """
    _validate_regularization(self.alpha, self.rcond)
    problem = build_least_squares_problem(
        states,
        targets,
        fit_intercept=self.bias is not None,
        use_float64=self.use_float64,
        gram_dtype=self.gram_dtype,
    )

    # Operate on the centered design matrix when an intercept is fitted so
    # the SVD sees the same problem the Gram-based solvers do. The means
    # carried by ``problem`` reproduce the analytic centering exactly.
    x = problem.X.to(problem.solve_dtype)
    y = problem.y.to(problem.solve_dtype)
    if problem.fit_intercept:
        assert problem.x_mean is not None and problem.y_mean is not None
        x = x - problem.x_mean.to(problem.solve_dtype)
        y = y - problem.y_mean.to(problem.solve_dtype)

    # Economy SVD of the (N, F) design matrix.
    u, s, vh = torch.linalg.svd(x, full_matrices=False)

    # Tikhonov filter factors s / (s^2 + alpha). For alpha == 0 this is
    # 1 / s on the retained singular values and 0 on those at/below the
    # rcond cutoff (the minimum-norm least-squares pseudo-inverse).
    if self.alpha > 0:
        filt = _ridge_filter(s, self.alpha)
    else:
        cutoff = self.rcond * s.max() if s.numel() > 0 else s.new_zeros(())
        retained = s > cutoff
        safe_s = torch.where(retained, s, torch.ones_like(s))
        inv_s = torch.where(retained, 1.0 / safe_s, torch.zeros_like(s))
        filt = inv_s

    # W = V diag(filt) Uᵀ y  with vh = Vᵀ, so V = vh.T.
    coefs = vh.T @ (filt.unsqueeze(1) * (u.T @ y))

    return finalize_fit(problem, coefs)

    PinvReadoutLayer(
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    rcond: float = 1e-15,
    solver: str = "lstsq",
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: dtype | None = None,
)

    Bases: ReadoutLayer

    Readout layer solved via least squares / pseudo-inverse.

    Solves the (optionally centered) least-squares problem min_W ||X W - Y|| directly, without forming the Gram matrix, using one of:

    • solver='lstsq' (default) — torch.linalg.lstsq with the gelsd driver, a divide-and-conquer SVD-based least-squares solver that returns the minimum-norm solution for rank-deficient X and honours the rcond cutoff.
    • solver='pinv' — form the Moore–Penrose pseudo-inverse torch.linalg.pinv(X, rcond=...) and apply it to Y. Equivalent in result but materialises the (F, N) pseudo-inverse explicitly.

    This is a pure least-squares readout: there is no Tikhonov penalty (alpha). Regularisation comes only from the rcond truncation of small singular values. If you need an explicit ridge penalty use RidgeReadoutLayer or SVDReadoutLayer (which exposes both alpha and rcond).

    Solver-selection guide
    • Reach for PinvReadoutLayer for unregularised least squares on a possibly rank-deficient design matrix when you want the minimum-norm solution and don't need a Tikhonov alpha.
    • solver='lstsq' (default) is the right choice almost always — it never materialises the pseudo-inverse. Use solver='pinv' only if you specifically want the pseudo-inverse matrix itself.
    • For an explicit ridge penalty, prefer SVDReadoutLayer (filter factors, alpha + rcond) or RidgeReadoutLayer (Cholesky, fast, full rank).
    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    in_features

    Size of input features (reservoir state dimension).

    TYPE: int

    out_features

    Size of output features (prediction dimension).

    TYPE: int

    bias

    Whether to include a bias term. When True the data is centered and an unpenalised intercept is recovered; when False the raw design matrix is used with no intercept.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    name

    Name for this readout layer. Used for identification in multi-readout architectures and as the key into targets by ESNTrainer.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

    trainable

    If True, weights are trainable via backpropagation.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    rcond

    Relative cutoff for small singular values. Singular values at or below rcond * s_max are dropped, making rank-deficient problems well posed.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-15

    solver

    Whether to solve with torch.linalg.lstsq or an explicit torch.linalg.pinv.

    TYPE: (lstsq, pinv) DEFAULT: 'lstsq'

    use_float64

    If True the least-squares solve runs in float64 and the result is cast back to the parameter dtype.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    gram_dtype

    Dtype for forming / casting the design matrix. Default None is the solve dtype (float64 with use_float64=True) on every device. No Gram matrix is formed; the decomposition operates directly on the design matrix.

    TYPE: dtype DEFAULT: None

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION

    Weight matrix of shape (out_features, in_features).

    TYPE: Parameter

    bias

    Bias vector of shape (out_features,), or None if bias=False.

    TYPE: Parameter or None

    rcond

    Relative singular-value cutoff.

    TYPE: float

    The selected least-squares solver.

>>> states = torch.randn(8, 50, 200)  # (batch, time, features)
>>> targets = torch.randn(8, 50, 3)
>>> readout.fit(states, targets)

    def __init__(
    self,
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    rcond: float = 1e-15,
    solver: str = "lstsq",
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias, name, trainable)
    if rcond < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"rcond must be non-negative, got {rcond}.")
    if solver not in self._VALID_SOLVERS:
        raise ValueError(f"solver must be one of {self._VALID_SOLVERS}, got {solver!r}.")
    self.rcond = rcond
    self.solver = solver
    self.use_float64 = use_float64
    self.gram_dtype = gram_dtype

    def solve(
    self,
    states: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
    """Solve the readout via least squares / pinv on flattened inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        Flattened state matrix of shape `(N, in_features)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Flattened target matrix of shape `(N, out_features)`.

    Returns
    -------
    coefs : torch.Tensor
        Coefficient matrix of shape `(in_features, out_features)`.
    intercept : torch.Tensor or None
        Intercept vector of shape `(out_features,)`, or `None` when the
        layer was built with `bias=False`.
    """
    # No Tikhonov penalty here: the normal-equations Gram is unused, so
    # build the problem only to share the centering / precision machinery.
    problem = build_least_squares_problem(
        states,
        targets,
        fit_intercept=self.bias is not None,
        use_float64=self.use_float64,
        gram_dtype=self.gram_dtype,
    )

    x = problem.X.to(problem.solve_dtype)
    y = problem.y.to(problem.solve_dtype)
    if problem.fit_intercept:
        assert problem.x_mean is not None and problem.y_mean is not None
        x = x - problem.x_mean.to(problem.solve_dtype)
        y = y - problem.y_mean.to(problem.solve_dtype)

    if self.solver == "lstsq" and x.device.type == "cpu":
        # gelsd is SVD-based and handles rank-deficient X with rcond, but
        # it is CPU-only — torch.linalg.lstsq on CUDA supports only the
        # full-rank ``gels`` driver, which silently mishandles rank
        # deficiency. On CUDA we therefore route ``lstsq`` through the
        # SVD-based pseudo-inverse, which is equally robust there.
        result = torch.linalg.lstsq(x, y, rcond=self.rcond, driver="gelsd")
        coefs = result.solution
    else:  # "pinv", or "lstsq" on a non-CPU device
        coefs = torch.linalg.pinv(x, rcond=self.rcond) @ y

    return finalize_fit(problem, coefs)

    IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer ¶

    IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer(
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    alpha: float = 1e-06,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: dtype | None = None,
)

    Bases: ReadoutLayer

    Readout layer that fits ridge regression incrementally over chunks.

    The classic readout fit requires every state in memory at once. This layer instead accumulates the ridge sufficient statistics as chunks arrive:

    • XtX / Xty — centered cross-products when bias=True and raw products when bias=False,
    • _mean_x / _mean_y — stable running means for the intercept,
    • sum_x / sum_y — retained column sums,
    • n — the running sample count.

    Centered chunk statistics are merged using the Chan covariance formula, so accumulating them chunk-by-chunk and solving once is algebraically identical to forming the whole Gram in a single pass. finalize assembles the centered, regularised normal equations from the running statistics and Cholesky-solves them, recovering the same coefficients (within floating point) that a full-batch CholeskyReadoutLayer / CGReadoutLayer fit would produce.

    The ridge objective is identical to the single-shot readouts,

    \[ \lVert X W - Y \rVert_2^2 + \alpha \lVert W \rVert_2^2 , \]

    with the intercept (when bias=True) recovered from the running means and left un-penalised, exactly as in the shared _solve_utils centering.

    Lifecycle
    1. (Optionally) reset_accumulators to clear any prior statistics.
    2. Call partial_fit once per chunk to accumulate statistics.
    3. Call finalize once to solve and write the fitted weights.

    is_fitted becomes True only after finalize; calling forward before that raises a clear RuntimeError.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    in_features

    Size of input features (reservoir state dimension).

    TYPE: int

    out_features

    Size of output features (prediction dimension).

    TYPE: int

    bias

    Whether to include a bias term. When True the running means center the data and an un-penalised intercept is recovered; when False the raw normal equations are solved with no intercept.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    name

    Name for this readout layer. Used for identification in multi-readout architectures and as the key into targets by ESNTrainer.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

    trainable

    If True, weights are trainable via backpropagation.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    alpha

    L2 regularization strength. Must be non-negative.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    use_float64

    If True the accumulator buffers and the small (F, F) solve run in float64 and the fitted weights are cast back to the parameter dtype. Parameter casts such as .float() preserve float64 working statistics. MPS cannot hold these statistics; use CPU or explicitly opt out with use_float64=False for supported MPS operations.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    gram_dtype

    Dtype the per-chunk Gram matmuls run in. Default None is automatic: the solve dtype (float64 with use_float64=True) on every device. Pass torch.float32 explicitly for faster, lower-precision Gram formation on CUDA when the feature matrix is well-conditioned.

    TYPE: dtype DEFAULT: None

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION
    weight

    Weight matrix of shape (out_features, in_features).

    TYPE: Parameter

    bias

    Bias vector of shape (out_features,), or None if bias=False.

    TYPE: Parameter or None

    alpha

    L2 regularization strength.

    TYPE: float

    n_seen

    Number of samples accumulated so far (across all chunks).

    TYPE: int

    Examples:

    Fit over three chunks of a long sequence then finalize:

    >>> readout = IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer(in_features=200, out_features=3)
>>> for states_chunk, targets_chunk in chunks:
...     readout.partial_fit(states_chunk, targets_chunk)
>>> readout.finalize()
>>> output = readout(states_chunk)
    See Also

    CholeskyReadoutLayer : Single-shot Cholesky ridge readout. CGReadoutLayer : Iterative Conjugate Gradient ridge readout. resdag.training.ESNTrainer.fit_stream : Trainer streaming-over-DataLoader path.

    def __init__(
    self,
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    alpha: float = 1e-6,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias, name, trainable)
    if alpha < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"alpha must be non-negative, got {alpha}.")
    self.alpha = alpha
    self.use_float64 = use_float64
    self.gram_dtype = gram_dtype

    # When True the forward guard is bypassed: the layer may run unfitted.
    # Used internally during graph construction (where ``pytorch_symbolic``
    # traces shapes by calling ``forward`` once) and during the trainer's
    # streaming accumulation pass (where ``forward`` only needs to flow a
    # value downstream while the pre-hook accumulates statistics). Never a
    # public attribute — genuine inference always goes through the guard.
    self._allow_unfitted_forward = False

    # Accumulator dtype: float64 when use_float64 (cheap on the small
    # (F, F) / (F, T) buffers and avoids drift across many chunks).
    acc_dtype = resolve_solve_dtype(self.weight.dtype, use_float64)
    # Persistent buffers so accumulation state survives state_dict
    # round-trips and rides along with .to(device) / .to(dtype).
    self.register_buffer("XtX", torch.zeros(in_features, in_features, dtype=acc_dtype))
    self.register_buffer("Xty", torch.zeros(in_features, out_features, dtype=acc_dtype))
    self.register_buffer("sum_x", torch.zeros(in_features, dtype=acc_dtype))
    self.register_buffer("sum_y", torch.zeros(out_features, dtype=acc_dtype))
    self.register_buffer("_mean_x", torch.zeros(in_features, dtype=acc_dtype))
    self.register_buffer("_mean_y", torch.zeros(out_features, dtype=acc_dtype))
    # Version 1 stores centered cross-products when bias=True. Legacy
    # checkpoints had no version and stored cancellation-prone raw moments.
    self.register_buffer("_statistics_version", torch.ones((), dtype=torch.long))
    self.register_buffer("_n", torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.long))

    # Dtype the per-chunk Gram matmuls actually ran in (resolved from the
    # first chunk in ``partial_fit``). Recorded so ``finalize``'s accuracy
    # guard weights its condition estimate by the right machine epsilon —
    # the precision loss happens at the float32 matmul, before the float64
    # accumulation, so the accumulator dtype would understate it.
    self._chunk_gram_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None

    n_seen: int

    @torch.no_grad()
def reset_accumulators(self) -> None:
    """Clear all accumulated statistics and the fitted flag.

    Returns the layer to its freshly-constructed state: the sufficient
    statistics are zeroed, the sample count is reset to `0`, and
    `is_fitted` becomes `False`. Call this before re-fitting a layer
    that was previously finalized.
    """
    self.XtX.zero_()
    self.Xty.zero_()
    self.sum_x.zero_()
    self.sum_y.zero_()
    self._mean_x.zero_()
    self._mean_y.zero_()
    self._n.zero_()
    self._chunk_gram_dtype = None
    self._set_fitted(False)

    @torch.no_grad()
def partial_fit(
    self, states: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor
) -> "IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer":
    """Accumulate the ridge sufficient statistics for one chunk.

    Flattens `(B, T, F)` chunks to `(N, F)`, validates shapes against
    the layer's feature dimensions, and adds the chunk's contribution to the
    running `XtX` / `Xty` / `sum_x` / `sum_y` / `n` accumulators.
    Call once per `DataLoader` batch (or per window of a long sequence);
    the centered statistics are merged so chunk boundaries do not affect the final
    fit.

    Calling `partial_fit` after `finalize` keeps accumulating onto
    the existing statistics and clears the fitted flag — the layer must be
    re-`finalize`\\ d before it can be used for inference again. Use
    `reset_accumulators` to start a fresh fit.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        State chunk of shape `(B, T, F_in)` or `(N, F_in)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Target chunk of shape `(B, T, F_out)` or `(N, F_out)`.

    Returns
    -------
    IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer
        `self`, so calls can be chained.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `states` and `targets` disagree on the sample dimension after
        flattening, if the state feature dimension does not match
        `in_features`, if the target feature dimension does not match
        `out_features`, or if `states` or `targets` contain non-finite
        (NaN or Inf) values.
    """
    states, targets = self._prepare_fit_inputs(states, targets, "partial_fit")

    # Form each chunk in the requested Gram dtype (float64 by default),
    # then merge into buffers in their independently configured working dtype.
    solve_dtype = resolve_solve_dtype(states.dtype, self.use_float64)
    gram_dtype = resolve_gram_dtype(states.dtype, states.device, solve_dtype, self.gram_dtype)
    self._chunk_gram_dtype = gram_dtype
    x = states.to(gram_dtype)
    y = targets.to(gram_dtype)

    acc_dtype = self.XtX.dtype
    if self.bias is not None:
        chunk_mean_x = x.mean(dim=0)
        chunk_mean_y = y.mean(dim=0)
        centered_x = x - chunk_mean_x
        centered_y = y - chunk_mean_y
        delta_x = chunk_mean_x.to(acc_dtype) - self._mean_x
        delta_y = chunk_mean_y.to(acc_dtype) - self._mean_y
        old_count = self._n.to(acc_dtype)
        total = old_count + states.shape[0]
        correction = old_count * states.shape[0] / total
        self.XtX.add_((centered_x.T @ centered_x).to(acc_dtype))
        self.Xty.add_((centered_x.T @ centered_y).to(acc_dtype))
        self.XtX.addmm_(delta_x[:, None], (correction * delta_x)[None, :])
        self.Xty.addmm_(delta_x[:, None], (correction * delta_y)[None, :])
        self._mean_x.add_(delta_x * (states.shape[0] / total))
        self._mean_y.add_(delta_y * (states.shape[0] / total))
    else:
        self.XtX += (x.T @ x).to(acc_dtype)
        self.Xty += (x.T @ y).to(acc_dtype)
    self.sum_x += x.sum(dim=0).to(acc_dtype)
    self.sum_y += y.sum(dim=0).to(acc_dtype)
    self._n += states.shape[0]

    # Any prior fit is stale once new data arrives.
    self._set_fitted(False)
    return self

    finalize ¶

    finalize() -> None

    Solve the accumulated ridge system and write the fitted weights.

    Assembles the centered (when bias=True), regularised normal equations (XᵀX + αI) W = Xᵀy from the running sufficient statistics and solves them with a Cholesky factorisation. Recovers the un-penalised intercept from the running means, copies the result into the layer's weight / bias parameters, and sets is_fitted to True.

    RAISES DESCRIPTION
    RuntimeError

    If no samples have been accumulated (partial_fit was never called, or reset_accumulators was called since).
    Notes

    finalize does not clear the accumulators, so it can be called again after additional partial_fit calls to refine the fit on more data. Call reset_accumulators to start over.

    @torch.no_grad()
def finalize(self) -> None:
    """Solve the accumulated ridge system and write the fitted weights.

    Assembles the centered (when `bias=True`), regularised normal
    equations `(XᵀX + αI) W = Xᵀy` from the running sufficient statistics
    and solves them with a Cholesky factorisation. Recovers the un-penalised
    intercept from the running means, copies the result into the layer's
    `weight` / `bias` parameters, and sets `is_fitted` to `True`.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        If no samples have been accumulated (`partial_fit` was never
        called, or `reset_accumulators` was called since).

    Notes
    -----
    `finalize` does **not** clear the accumulators, so it can be called
    again after additional `partial_fit` calls to refine the fit on
    more data. Call `reset_accumulators` to start over.
    """
    n = self.n_seen
    if n == 0:
        readout_id = f"'{self._name}'" if self._name is not None else type(self).__name__
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}.finalize({readout_id}): no data accumulated. "
            f"Call partial_fit(states, targets) at least once before finalize()."
        )

    fit_intercept = self.bias is not None
    gram = self.XtX
    rhs = self.Xty

    layer_name = (
        f"{type(self).__name__}('{self._name}')"
        if self._name is not None
        else type(self).__name__
    )
    coefs = solve_ridge(  # (F, T)
        gram,
        rhs,
        self.alpha,
        layer_name=layer_name,
        gram_dtype=self._chunk_gram_dtype,
    )

    intercept = None
    if fit_intercept and self.bias is not None:
        intercept = self._mean_y - self._mean_x @ coefs
    self._copy_coefficients(coefs, intercept)

    self._set_fitted(True)

    def solve(
    self,
    states: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
    """Single-shot fit: accumulate one chunk then finalize.

    Provided so `IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer` is a drop-in
    `ReadoutLayer` — `fit(states, targets)` works exactly like the
    other readouts (it resets the accumulators, accumulates the whole batch,
    and solves). The hook returns the fitted coefficients so the base
    `fit` copy-back path is reused.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        Flattened state matrix of shape `(N, in_features)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Flattened target matrix of shape `(N, out_features)`.

    Returns
    -------
    coefs : torch.Tensor
        Coefficient matrix of shape `(in_features, out_features)`.
    intercept : torch.Tensor or None
        Intercept vector of shape `(out_features,)`, or `None` when the
        layer was built with `bias=False`.
    """
    self.reset_accumulators()
    self.partial_fit(states, targets)
    self.finalize()
    # ``finalize`` already wrote the parameters and flipped is_fitted; hand
    # the base ``fit`` the same values so its copy-back is a harmless no-op.
    coefs = self.weight.T.to(states.dtype)
    intercept = None if self.bias is None else self.bias.to(states.dtype)
    return coefs, intercept

    forward(input: Tensor) -> Tensor

    Apply the fitted linear transformation to input.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    input

    Input tensor of shape (B, F) or (B, T, F).

    TYPE: Tensor

    RETURNS DESCRIPTION
    Tensor

    Output tensor of shape (B, F_out) or (B, T, F_out).
    RAISES DESCRIPTION
    RuntimeError

    If finalize has not been called since the last partial_fit / construction. The error names the layer and points at finalize() so the streaming lifecycle is unambiguous.
    Notes

    Two internal call sites legitimately run forward while unfitted and bypass the guard via the private _allow_unfitted_forward flag: pytorch_symbolic graph construction (which traces output shapes by calling forward once with placeholder data) and the trainer's streaming accumulation pass (where the readout's forward only flows a value downstream while a pre-hook accumulates statistics). Genuine inference always goes through the guard.

    Under torch.compile (the compiled forecast fast path captures this forward directly and calls it per autoregressive step) the entire Python guard is skipped: it would otherwise force a dynamo graph break on every step and silently drop the model to the ~14x-slower eager rollout. Fittedness is still enforced before the compiled loop by the eager teacher-forced warmup pass that forecast always runs first: it executes the full graph — including this readout's eager forward — which trips the guard for a genuinely-unfitted readout. So skipping the per-step guard under compile removes a redundant check, not a safety net. The fittedness check itself reads the sync-free _fitted_flag mirror (see resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer.is_fitted), never the _is_fitted buffer's .item(), so even the eager per-step path pays no device->host sync.

    def forward(self, input: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Apply the fitted linear transformation to `input`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    input : torch.Tensor
        Input tensor of shape `(B, F)` or `(B, T, F)`.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Output tensor of shape `(B, F_out)` or `(B, T, F_out)`.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        If `finalize` has not been called since the last
        `partial_fit` / construction. The error names the layer and points
        at `finalize()` so the streaming lifecycle is unambiguous.

    Notes
    -----
    Two internal call sites legitimately run `forward` while unfitted and
    bypass the guard via the private `_allow_unfitted_forward` flag:
    `pytorch_symbolic` graph construction (which traces output shapes by
    calling `forward` once with placeholder data) and the trainer's
    streaming accumulation pass (where the readout's forward only flows a
    value downstream while a pre-hook accumulates statistics). Genuine
    inference always goes through the guard.

    Under `torch.compile` (the compiled forecast fast path captures this
    `forward` directly and calls it per autoregressive step) the entire
    Python guard is skipped: it would otherwise force a dynamo graph break
    on every step and silently drop the model to the ~14x-slower eager
    rollout. Fittedness is still enforced **before** the compiled loop by the
    eager teacher-forced warmup pass that `forecast` always runs first: it
    executes the full graph — including this readout's eager `forward` —
    which trips the guard for a genuinely-unfitted readout. So skipping the
    per-step guard under compile removes a redundant check, not a safety net.
    The fittedness check itself reads the sync-free `_fitted_flag` mirror
    (see `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer.is_fitted`), never the
    `_is_fitted` buffer's `.item()`, so even the eager per-step path
    pays no device->host sync.
    """
    # Compiled fast path: never let dynamo trace the guard (a graph break
    # per step forfeits the compiled forecast). The eager warmup pass that
    # forecast runs first already trips the guard for an unfitted readout,
    # so skipping the per-step guard under compile is safe here.
    if torch.compiler.is_compiling():
        return super().forward(input)

    # Eager path: the fitted bool read is sync-free; the frame walk (the
    # expensive part) only runs when genuinely unfitted, i.e. rarely.
    if not self._fitted_flag and not self._allow_unfitted_forward and not _in_symbolic_build():
        readout_id = f"'{self._name}'" if self._name is not None else type(self).__name__
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}({readout_id}) is not fitted: call finalize() after "
            f"partial_fit(...) before forward/inference. "
            f"({self.n_seen} sample(s) accumulated so far.)"
        )
    return super().forward(input)

    RLSReadout ¶

    RLSReadout(
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    *,
    forgetting: float = 1.0,
    delta: float | None = None,
    alpha: float | None = None,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    device: device | None = None,
    dtype: dtype | None = None
)

    Bases: ReadoutLayer

    True-online Recursive Least Squares (RLS) readout with forgetting.

    Refines the readout weights one sample at a time from a running inverse-correlation matrix \(P\), instead of solving a batch linear system. This makes it the natural readout for streaming and non-stationary reservoir computing: samples can arrive indefinitely, and a forgetting factor \(\lambda < 1\) lets the readout track a target whose statistics drift over time.

    Update equations

    For each feature vector \(x_t \in \mathbb{R}^F\) with target \(d_t \in \mathbb{R}^O\), writing \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{F \times O}\) for the transpose of the nn.Linear weight and \(P \in \mathbb{R}^{F \times F}\) for the inverse correlation:

    \[ \begin{aligned} g_t &= P_{t-1}\, x_t \\ k_t &= g_t / (\lambda + x_t^\top g_t) \\ e_t &= d_t - W_{t-1}^\top x_t \\ W_t &= W_{t-1} + k_t\, e_t^\top \\ P_t &= (P_{t-1} - k_t\, g_t^\top) / \lambda \end{aligned} \]

    The a-priori error \(e_t\) uses the current weights (before this step's update), which is what makes the recursion equivalent to an exponentially-weighted least-squares solve at every step. The rank-1 \(P\) update preserves symmetry in exact arithmetic, so \(P\) is re-symmetrised periodically — every _RESYM_EVERY steps plus once at the end of each pass — to control floating-point drift without paying a full transpose-copy on every step.

    Relationship to ridge
    • \(\lambda = 1\) (the default) is growing-window RLS: every past sample keeps unit weight, so after enough data the fit converges to the ordinary least-squares solution — equivalently ridge with \(\alpha \to 0\), the \(\delta\) prior washing out as evidence accumulates. A fully-streamed \(\lambda = 1\) fit therefore agrees with a batch RidgeReadoutLayer (small alpha) fit on the same data to a tight tolerance.
    • \(\lambda < 1\) forgets: sample \(t - \tau\) is weighted \(\lambda^{\tau}\), giving an effective memory of \(1 / (1 - \lambda)\) samples. Use it when the input/target relation is non-stationary; there is no batch-ridge equivalent.

    Because RLS is inherently sequential (each \(P_t\), \(W_t\) depends on its predecessor), partial_fit applies the updates in row-major stream order: a (B, T, F) batch is flattened to (B * T, F) and consumed one step at a time, exactly as ReadoutLayer.fit flattens.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    in_features

    Size of input features F (reservoir state dimension).

    TYPE: int

    out_features

    Size of output features O (prediction dimension).

    TYPE: int

    bias

    Whether to include a bias term. When True a constant 1 feature is appended to every input internally, so the intercept is estimated by the same RLS recursion as the slopes (and, like the slopes, is subject to the \(\delta\) prior — it is not separately un-penalised as in the centered batch solvers). When False no intercept is fitted.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    name

    Name for this readout layer. Used for identification in multi-readout architectures and as the key into targets by ESNTrainer.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

    trainable

    If True, weights are trainable via backpropagation after fitting.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    forgetting

    The forgetting factor \(\lambda \in (0, 1]\). 1.0 is growing-window RLS (converges to ordinary least squares); values < 1 exponentially forget old samples to track non-stationarity. Must be in (0, 1].

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

    delta

    Initialises \(P = I / \delta\) (default 1e-2 when neither delta nor alpha is given). Acts as a soft ridge prior on the early, data-starved updates: a larger delta shrinks the initial weights harder (a stronger prior), a smaller delta trusts the first samples more. Must be positive. Aliased by alpha — see below.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: None

    alpha

    Alias for delta (the two name the same ridge-prior knob: \(P_0 = I / \alpha\)). Ridge readouts spell this regularisation strength alpha, so it is accepted here too for API symmetry. Passing both alpha and a non-default delta raises. Must be positive.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: None

    use_float64

    If True the P recursion and the weight updates run in float64 (the fitted parameters are cast back to the layer dtype). The rank-1 \(P\) update accumulates round-off over many steps, so double precision materially improves stability; it is cheap because the per-step work is only O(F^2). Parameter casts such as .float() preserve this working precision. MPS does not support float64 statistics; use CPU or explicitly opt out with use_float64=False for supported lower-precision operations.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    device

    Device for the layer parameters and the P buffer.

    TYPE: device DEFAULT: None

    dtype

    Dtype for the nn.Linear parameters.

    TYPE: dtype DEFAULT: None

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION
    weight

    Weight matrix of shape (out_features, in_features).

    TYPE: Parameter

    bias

    Bias vector of shape (out_features,), or None if bias=False.

    TYPE: Parameter or None

    P

    The (F', F') inverse-correlation buffer, where F' = F + 1 when a bias is fitted (the appended constant feature) and F otherwise. A persistent buffer, so it rides along with state_dict / .to(...).

    TYPE: Tensor

    forgetting

    The forgetting factor \(\lambda\).

    TYPE: float

    delta

    The \(P\) initialisation constant.

    TYPE: float

    n_seen

    Number of samples applied across all partial_fit calls since the last reset.

    TYPE: int

    Examples:

    Stream a stationary problem to convergence, then predict:

    >>> readout = RLSReadout(in_features=200, out_features=3, forgetting=1.0)
>>> for states_chunk, targets_chunk in chunks:
...     readout.partial_fit(states_chunk, targets_chunk)
>>> output = readout(states_chunk)

    Fresh online fit in one call (resets P first):

    >>> readout.fit_online(states, targets)
    See Also

    IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer : Streaming ridge via sufficient statistics. RidgeReadoutLayer : Batch closed-form ridge readout. resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer that uses this for fitting.

    References

    [1] S. Haykin, "Adaptive Filter Theory," 5th ed., Pearson, 2014, ch. 10.

    def __init__(
    self,
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    *,
    forgetting: float = 1.0,
    delta: float | None = None,
    alpha: float | None = None,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    device: torch.device | None = None,
    dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias, name, trainable)
    if device is not None or dtype is not None:
        # nn.Linear does not forward device/dtype in the resdag readout
        # signature, so move the freshly-created parameters explicitly. This
        # keeps the constructor signature aligned with the family's
        # device/dtype ergonomics without materialising a second Linear.
        self.to(device=device, dtype=dtype)

    if not 0.0 < forgetting <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"forgetting (lambda) must be in (0, 1], got {forgetting}.")
    # ``alpha`` is an alias for ``delta`` (both parameterise P_0 = I / delta).
    # ``delta`` defaults to ``None`` (sentinel for "unset") so passing both
    # explicitly is detectable and rejected; the documented default is 1e-2.
    if alpha is not None and delta is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            "Pass either 'alpha' or 'delta' to RLSReadout, not both "
            f"(got alpha={alpha}, delta={delta}); they name the same "
            "P-initialisation knob P_0 = I / delta."
        )
    if alpha is not None:
        delta = alpha
    if delta is None:
        delta = 1e-2
    if delta <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"delta (alpha) must be positive, got {delta}.")

    self.forgetting = forgetting
    self.delta = delta
    self.use_float64 = use_float64

    # The RLS recursion runs over an augmented feature space when a bias is
    # fitted: a constant 1 is appended to every input so the intercept is
    # learned by the same recursion. P therefore has size F' = F (+ 1).
    self._p_dim = in_features + 1 if self.bias is not None else in_features
    recur_dtype = resolve_solve_dtype(self.weight.dtype, use_float64)
    self.register_buffer(
        "P",
        torch.eye(self._p_dim, dtype=recur_dtype, device=self.weight.device) / self.delta,
    )
    self.register_buffer("_n", torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.long, device=self.weight.device))
    # A fresh partial_fit stream has the same zero coefficient prior as
    # fit_online/reset_state, including in unobserved feature directions.
    self.reset_state()

    reset_state ¶

    reset_state() -> None

    Reset the recursion: P = I / delta, zero the weights and sample count.

    Returns the layer to its freshly-constructed online state — P is reinitialised to I / delta, the weight / bias parameters are zeroed, the sample count is cleared, and is_fitted becomes False. Call this before starting a fresh stream; fit_online calls it for you.

    @torch.no_grad()
def reset_state(self) -> None:
    """Reset the recursion: `P = I / delta`, zero the weights and sample count.

    Returns the layer to its freshly-constructed online state — `P` is
    reinitialised to `I / delta`, the `weight` / `bias` parameters are
    zeroed, the sample count is cleared, and `is_fitted` becomes
    `False`. Call this before starting a fresh stream; `fit_online`
    calls it for you.
    """
    eye = torch.eye(self._p_dim, dtype=self.P.dtype, device=self.P.device)
    self.P.copy_(eye / self.delta)
    self.weight.zero_()
    if self.bias is not None:
        self.bias.zero_()
    self._n.zero_()
    self._set_fitted(False)

    partial_fit(states: Tensor, targets: Tensor) -> RLSReadout

    Apply the RLS recursion over one chunk, continuing the current stream.

    Flattens a (B, T, F) chunk to (N, F) (row-major, matching ReadoutLayer.fit), validates shapes and finiteness, and runs the rank-1 RLS update once per sample in stream order. State (P and the weights) is carried across calls, so feeding a long sequence in chunks is identical to feeding it whole — call reset_state (or fit_online) to start a fresh stream.

    self, so calls can be chained.

    ValueError

    If states and targets disagree on the sample dimension after flattening, if the state feature dimension does not match in_features, if the target feature dimension does not match out_features, or if states or targets contain non-finite (NaN or Inf) values.

    @torch.no_grad()
def partial_fit(self, states: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor) -> "RLSReadout":
    """Apply the RLS recursion over one chunk, continuing the current stream.

    Flattens a `(B, T, F)` chunk to `(N, F)` (row-major, matching
    `ReadoutLayer.fit`), validates shapes and finiteness, and runs the
    rank-1 RLS update once per sample in stream order. State (`P` and
    the weights) is **carried across calls**, so feeding a long sequence in
    chunks is identical to feeding it whole — call `reset_state` (or
    `fit_online`) to start a fresh stream.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        State chunk of shape `(B, T, F_in)` or `(N, F_in)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Target chunk of shape `(B, T, F_out)` or `(N, F_out)`.

    Returns
    -------
    RLSReadout
        `self`, so calls can be chained.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `states` and `targets` disagree on the sample dimension after
        flattening, if the state feature dimension does not match
        `in_features`, if the target feature dimension does not match
        `out_features`, or if `states` or `targets` contain non-finite
        (NaN or Inf) values.
    """
    states, targets = self._validate_chunk(states, targets, "partial_fit")
    self._rls_update(states, targets)
    # RLS refines the actual weights every step, so the layer is usable for
    # inference the moment any data has been applied.
    self._set_fitted(True)
    return self

    @torch.no_grad()
def fit_online(self, states: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor) -> "RLSReadout":
    """Reset the recursion and stream-fit the whole `(states, targets)` pair.

    A readable one-call entry point that mirrors
    `IncrementalRidgeReadoutLayer`'s ergonomics: it clears any prior
    recursion state (`reset_state`) and then `partial_fit`\\ s the
    full input. Use it for a fresh online fit over a single sequence; use
    `partial_fit` directly to continue an existing stream.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        State matrix of shape `(B, T, F_in)` or `(N, F_in)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Target matrix of shape `(B, T, F_out)` or `(N, F_out)`.

    Returns
    -------
    RLSReadout
        `self`, so calls can be chained.
    """
    self.reset_state()
    return self.partial_fit(states, targets)

    Single-shot batch fit: reset the recursion and stream the whole pass.

    Provided so RLSReadout is a drop-in ReadoutLayer — fit(states, targets) (and hence ESNTrainer) works exactly like the other readouts. This is the honest single-shot behaviour for an online algorithm: it resets P and applies the RLS recursion over the entire (already-flattened) batch once, in stream order. For \(\lambda = 1\) and enough samples this recovers the ordinary least-squares fit; it is not a closed-form ridge solve.

    def solve(
    self,
    states: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
    """Single-shot batch fit: reset the recursion and stream the whole pass.

    Provided so `RLSReadout` is a drop-in `ReadoutLayer` —
    `fit(states, targets)` (and hence `ESNTrainer`) works exactly
    like the other readouts. This is the *honest* single-shot behaviour for
    an online algorithm: it resets `P` and applies the RLS recursion over
    the entire (already-flattened) batch once, in stream order. For
    $\\lambda = 1$ and enough samples this recovers the ordinary
    least-squares fit; it is **not** a closed-form ridge solve.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : torch.Tensor
        Flattened state matrix of shape `(N, in_features)`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Flattened target matrix of shape `(N, out_features)`.

    Returns
    -------
    coefs : torch.Tensor
        Coefficient matrix of shape `(in_features, out_features)`.
    intercept : torch.Tensor or None
        Intercept vector of shape `(out_features,)`, or `None` when the
        layer was built with `bias=False`.
    """
    # The base ``fit`` has already flattened + validated, but reset the
    # recursion so a batch ``fit`` is a clean, order-independent restart.
    self.reset_state()
    self._rls_update(states, targets)
    self._set_fitted(True)
    # ``_rls_update`` already wrote the parameters; hand the base ``fit`` the
    # same values so its copy-back is a harmless no-op.
    coefs = self.weight.detach().T.to(states.dtype)
    intercept = None if self.bias is None else self.bias.detach().to(states.dtype)
    return coefs, intercept

    FISTAReadoutLayer ¶

    FISTAReadoutLayer(
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    *,
    alpha: float = 0.001,
    l1_ratio: float = 1.0,
    max_iter: int = 1000,
    tol: float = 1e-06,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: dtype | None = None,
    power_iters: int = 0,
    power_iter_margin: float = 0.05
)

    Bases: ReadoutLayer

    Sparse / robust readout via L1 (lasso) or elastic-net FISTA.

    Solves the elastic-net least-squares problem

    \[ \min_W \; \lVert X W - Y \rVert_2^2 + \alpha\,\rho\,\lVert W \rVert_1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\alpha\,(1-\rho)\,\lVert W \rVert_2^2 \]

    (rho = l1_ratio) with the accelerated proximal-gradient method FISTA [1], batched across every output column simultaneously. l1_ratio=1 gives pure lasso (maximally sparse); l1_ratio=0 gives pure ridge, in which case FISTA converges to the same solution as RidgeReadoutLayer. The intercept is recovered by centering and is left un-penalised.

    Objective and sklearn parameterisation

    This layer minimises the un-normalised sum-of-squares objective above. sklearn.linear_model.ElasticNet instead minimises a sample-size-normalised objective:

    \[ \frac{1}{2 N} \lVert X w - y \rVert_2^2 + \alpha_{\mathrm{sk}}\,\rho\,\lVert w \rVert_1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\alpha_{\mathrm{sk}}\,(1-\rho)\,\lVert w \rVert_2^2 , \]

    and sklearn.linear_model.Lasso(alpha=a) is the l1_ratio=1 special case, i.e. it minimises \(\tfrac{1}{2N}\lVert X w - y\rVert^2 + a\,\lVert w\rVert_1\).

    Multiplying sklearn's objective by 2 N shows the two objectives coincide when

    \[ \alpha_{\text{resdag}} = 2 N \, \alpha_{\mathrm{sk}} , \]

    where N is the number of (flattened) samples. So to reproduce a Lasso(alpha=a) / ElasticNet(alpha=a, l1_ratio=rho) fit with this layer, pass alpha = 2 * N * a (and the same l1_ratio). This scaling is what makes the FISTA coefficients match sklearn's to solver tolerance; see the tests for the round-trip.

    FISTA details

    The smooth part \(f(W) = \lVert X W - Y\rVert^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha(1-\rho)\lVert W\rVert^2\) has gradient \(2 X^\top X W - 2 X^\top Y + \alpha(1-\rho) W\), and the non-smooth L1 part has the soft-threshold proximal operator \(\operatorname{prox}(Z) = \operatorname{sign}(Z)\max(|Z| - \tau, 0)\) with threshold \(\tau = \text{step}\cdot\alpha\,\rho\). The constant step size is \(1/L\) with Lipschitz constant

    \[ L = 2\,\lambda_{\max}(X^\top X) + \alpha\,(1-\rho) , \]

    where \(\lambda_{\max}\) is the top eigenvalue of the Gram, obtained from torch.linalg.eigvalsh (small (F, F) system) or, when power_iters > 0, a few power iterations. Momentum follows the standard recurrence \(t_{k+1} = (1 + \sqrt{1 + 4 t_k^2})/2\). Iteration stops on the relative change \(\lVert W_{k+1} - W_k\rVert / \lVert W_k\rVert < \text{tol}\) or after max_iter steps (a non-converged run warns).

    Only the Gram \(X^\top X\) and \(X^\top Y\) enter the iteration, so the per-step cost is one (F, F) @ (F, T) matmul independent of the sample count N — cheap for the readout widths typical of reservoir computing.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    in_features

    Size of input features (reservoir state dimension).

    TYPE: int

    out_features

    Size of output features (prediction dimension).

    TYPE: int

    bias

    Whether to include a bias term. When True the data is centered and an unpenalised intercept is recovered; when False the raw normal equations are used with no intercept.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    name

    Name for this readout layer. Used for identification in multi-readout architectures and as the key into targets by ESNTrainer.

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

    trainable

    If True, weights are trainable via backpropagation.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    alpha

    Overall regularisation strength (must be non-negative). See the parameterisation note above for the relation to sklearn's alpha. alpha == 0 reduces to ordinary least squares (via FISTA).

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-3

    l1_ratio

    Elastic-net mixing in [0, 1]. 1.0 is pure lasso, 0.0 is pure ridge, values in between blend the two.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

    max_iter

    Maximum number of FISTA iterations.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: 1000

    tol

    Relative-change convergence tolerance on the coefficient matrix. A run that reaches max_iter without meeting it emits a RuntimeWarning.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    use_float64

    If True the iteration runs in float64 and the result is cast back to the parameter dtype.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    gram_dtype

    Dtype for forming the Gram matrix and right-hand side (the heavy (N, F) matmuls). Default None forms the Gram in the solve dtype (float64 unless use_float64=False) on every device; pass torch.float32 to opt into faster, lower-precision GPU Gram formation.

    TYPE: dtype DEFAULT: None

    power_iters

    If > 0, estimate the top Gram eigenvalue with this many power iterations instead of the exact torch.linalg.eigvalsh. The estimate is scaled up by (1 + power_iter_margin) to initialize the step size. Backtracking verifies the quadratic majorizer before each update; the margin alone is not a guaranteed spectral upper bound.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: 0

    power_iter_margin

    Initial margin applied to a power-iteration eigenvalue estimate.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.05

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION
    weight

    Weight matrix of shape (out_features, in_features).

    TYPE: Parameter

    bias

    Bias vector of shape (out_features,), or None if bias=False.

    TYPE: Parameter or None

    alpha

    Overall regularisation strength.

    TYPE: float

    l1_ratio

    Elastic-net mixing parameter.

    TYPE: float

    n_iter_

    Number of FISTA iterations run by the last fit (0 before the first fit).

    TYPE: int

    converged_

    Whether the last fit met the tol stopping criterion.

    TYPE: bool

    Examples:

    >>> readout = FISTAReadoutLayer(in_features=200, out_features=3, alpha=1e-2)
>>> states = torch.randn(8, 50, 200)  # (batch, time, features)
>>> targets = torch.randn(8, 50, 3)
>>> readout.fit(states, targets)
>>> output = readout(states)
>>> output.shape
torch.Size([8, 50, 3])
    See Also

    RidgeReadoutLayer : Direct ridge (L2-only) readout. SVDReadoutLayer : SVD filter-factor readout. resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer that uses this for fitting.

    References

    [1] A. Beck and M. Teboulle, "A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems," SIAM J. Imaging Sci., 2(1), 183-202, 2009.

    def __init__(
    self,
    in_features: int,
    out_features: int,
    bias: bool = True,
    name: str | None = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    *,
    alpha: float = 1e-3,
    l1_ratio: float = 1.0,
    max_iter: int = 1000,
    tol: float = 1e-6,
    use_float64: bool = True,
    gram_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
    power_iters: int = 0,
    power_iter_margin: float = 0.05,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias, name, trainable)
    if alpha < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"alpha must be non-negative, got {alpha}.")
    if not 0.0 <= l1_ratio <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"l1_ratio must be in [0, 1], got {l1_ratio}.")
    if max_iter < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"max_iter must be >= 1, got {max_iter}.")
    if tol < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"tol must be non-negative, got {tol}.")
    if power_iters < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"power_iters must be non-negative, got {power_iters}.")
    if power_iter_margin < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"power_iter_margin must be non-negative, got {power_iter_margin}.")
    self.alpha = alpha
    self.l1_ratio = l1_ratio
    self.max_iter = max_iter
    self.tol = tol
    self.use_float64 = use_float64
    self.gram_dtype = gram_dtype
    self.power_iters = power_iters
    self.power_iter_margin = power_iter_margin
    # Diagnostics populated by solve.
    self.n_iter_: int = 0
    self.converged_: bool = False
